title: From quantum universe to QOU: $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ verification
html:
Example. From quantum universe to QOU: \mathrm{SU}(2) verification

We verify the structural properties of the main theorem for G = \mathrm{SU}(2), extending Yekutieli lifting for SU(2).

Hypotheses. The quantum universe is (\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau) with substrate parameter q (SU(2) QOU). Observability holds: \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 because \mathrm{Ad}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) has no trivial sub-representation. The adjoint representation is irreducible.

(1) Descent terminates. The center of the endomorphism algebra is Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)) \cong \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))^{\mathrm{SU}(2)}. This ring of \mathrm{SU}(2)-invariant functions has Krull dimension \mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 1. The geometric descent tower is:

  \mathbb{CP}^1  \longrightarrow  \mathrm{pt},

which terminates in 1 step. At each step, the G_q-action is faithful. Observability ensures strict dimension reduction.

(2) First obstruction equals the Euler class. The obstruction \kappa_0 \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} equals the Euler class of the Reeb bundle. For the Hopf fibration, this is c_1(\text{Hopf}) = 1. Under the trace map:

  \kappa_0  \longmapsto  \chi(A)
  =  \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A)
  =  \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) =  2.

(3) Perpetual obstruction. We established that \kappa_0 = 1 \in \mathbb{Z} is non-torsion. The jet corrections at level n are non-negative. We have \kappa_n \geq 1 > 0 for all n \geq 0. The gerbe tower is perpetually obstructed.

(4) Branch point formula. The projective line object is \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathbb{CP}^1. The descent map \mathbb{CP}^1 \to \mathbb{CP}^1 has degree d = 1. The Riemann--Hurwitz formula gives:

  R_{\mathrm{tot}} =  2d + |\chi(A)|
  =  2 \cdot 1 + |2| =  4,

with B = 2 branch points (the north and south poles of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2). Each has ramification index e = 2.

(5) Terminal fiber data. At each branch point p \in \{0, \infty\} \subset \mathbb{CP}^1, the QOU reduces to fiber data (\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau, q(p)) with the involution:

  \sigma \colon \mathbb{CP}^1
   \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{Ad}(\mathrm{SU}(2))
  =  \mathfrak{su}(2).

This embedding realizes \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2 as the unit sphere in \mathfrak{su}(2) \cong \mathbb{R}^3. At the north pole p = 0, the involution acts as \sigma(v) = e_3 v e_3^{-1}. This is the identity on \mathrm{U}(1)-invariant sections and negation on off-diagonal components. The fiber data at p = \infty is conjugate via the Weyl group element w \colon e_3 \mapsto -e_3.

Conclusion. All five properties hold for \mathrm{SU}(2). The quantum universe (\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau) with observability and the Quantum lifting condition is a quantum observable universe. Descent terminates in 1 step, the brane tower is perpetually obstructed, there are 2 branch points on \mathbb{CP}^1, and the fiber data is governed by the adjoint embedding S^2 \hookrightarrow \mathfrak{su}(2).
